To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a general approach for the fabrication of polyvalent meso‐porous silica nanoparticle‐aptamer bio‐conjugates that target breast cancer cells.
polyvalent mesporous silica nanoparticle‐aptamer bio conjugates were designed, constructed and characterized.
polyvalent mesostructured silica nanoparticle‐aptamer biohybrids were designed to target nucleolin‐positive cancer cells and to deliver anticancer agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of multifunctional mesoporous silica nanoparticles that have the ability to target and deliver drugs to specific cancer cells.
the development of a novel drug delivery system for cancer therapy.
the development of novel polyvalent aptamer‐conjugated nanocarriers for the spatiotemporal delivery of therapeutic agents to cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a general strategy to fabricate polyvalent mesostructured silica nanoparticle‐aptamer biofunctionalized nanocarriers, which can specifically target nucleolin overexpressing cancer cells and deliver drugs to the cancer cells.
the combination of DNA aptamer targeting with mesoporous silica nanoparticles is a promising approach for cancer therapy and drug delivery.
the bioconjugate‐mediated cancer cell targeting and drug release can be effectively regulated by the aptamer‐mediated endocytosis and the pH‐responsive gate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of aptamers with mesoporous silica nanoparticles provides a promising approach for cancer‐specific targeted drug delivery.
we successfully constructed a novel polyvalent mesostructured silica nanoparticle‐aptamer bio‐conjugate, which is able to specifically target breast cancer cell lines.
we have successfully designed and fabricated polyvalent meso‐porous silica nanocarrier‐aptamer bio‐conjugates, which are able to effectively deliver drugs and target cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of aptamers with mesoporous nanocarriers can be used to develop a new class of targeted drug delivery systems for cancer treatment.
the combination of DNA aptamer and mesoporous nanoparticles can be a promising platform for the design and fabrication of controlled release drug delivery nanosystems.
the use of aptamers as targeting ligands can be combined with the use of mesoporous silica nanoparticles as drug carriers to achieve a targeted delivery system.
